purpose: The runtime the legacy golden fixtures were drawn on. Recorded so that the legacy goldens have a named profile and so that nobody mistakes them for evidence about this profile or any other. It cannot host the installed original, so it certifies nothing.
why_unsupported: The pinned DESCRIPTION declares Depends: R (>= 4.5.0). This runtime is R 4.3.3. Measured: `R CMD INSTALL --library=<tmp> reference/ANCOMBC` exits 1 with `ERROR: this R is version 4.3.3, package 'ANCOMBC' requires R >= 4.5.0`. There is no installed original on this runtime, therefore no original-vs-candidate byte comparison can be made here at all.
what_it_may_still_be_used_for: Explaining why the committed goldens under validation/golden are not a certificate for linux-r453-openblas: they were drawn on a different BLAS.
Re-running the *candidate* deterministically. That is Rust-vs-Rust evidence and never establishes equality with the original.

provisioning.note: Not provisioned by this project; it is what the host shipped.

runtime.interpreter_note: The system R declares no ANCOMBC in any of its libraries, so `original.installed` fails. That is the correct preflight result for this profile and is why it is marked unsupported rather than excluded from the verifier.

oracle.imports:
stats, DescTools, Hmisc, MASS, Matrix, Rdpack, doParallel,
doRNG, energy, foreach, gtools, lme4, lmerTest, multcomp,
nloptr, parallel, utils, quadprog
oracle.installed_library: <none: R 4.3.3 is below the pinned floor>

host.core_requirement_note: P5 needs >= 16 physical cores (ENV-1); this host has 8 on every profile.

certification_note: Never to be certified as an exactness profile on this runtime. To make it usable, install R >= 4.5.0 with reference BLAS, or lower the pinned Depends -- which would change the compatibility target and is not authorised.
